Julia — attached are our proposed redlines focused on a clear, implementable training exclusion plus definitions. Key callouts in the redline:

1) "Training" vs "Improvement": we separate "training" (retraining/fine-tuning of base model weights) from "quality improvement processes" (e.g., ephemeral prompt-based feedback used to improve query routing or heuristics). The customer opt-out blocks the former.

2) "Derivative outputs" definition: we propose: "Derivative outputs" means text, embeddings, or other content generated by the Services that is functionally derived from Customer Data; such outputs shall not be used to train, fine-tune or update any model or training corpus without Customer's prior written consent.

3) Auditability: Redwood will provide quarterly export of invocation logs and a one-time export of KV caches on request for compliance review.

Attachment: DPA_Northpoint_redlines_v1.docx

If these redlines look good, we can route to our Ops team for implementation notes and then send to DocuSign.

Alex — quick answers from Engineering:

- Allowed "quality improvement" examples we can list explicitly: request routing heuristics, cache TTL adjustments, rate-limit feedback loops, and anonymized metrics used to size autoscaler decisions. None of these touch model weights or training corpora when the customer has selected a no-training opt-out.
- Monthly invocation log exports: doable; we'll need an automated job and an S3 location (or secure FTP) you can provide.
- Subprocessors: any subprocessors that would handle Customer Data will be contractually bound by the same no-training restriction; we will flow that requirement into subprocessor agreements and provide a subprocessor roster.

Tradeoffs to call out: customers who opt out of training may see slightly higher per-token costs because we cannot safely reuse anonymous prefixes for model improvement projects; caching and batching optimizations at the model-improvement layer will be disabled. Latency impact should be modest (median +10-20ms) but we'll document it.

Happy to have a technical call to walk through specifics.

Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
